addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - API usage, tool use, Anthropic SDK usage. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- qemu-runner: Use this agent when you need to run a RISC-V ELF binary through Andes QEMU and get its output. Always use this agent instead of running QEMU directly, as it handles the semihosting fd 9 output capture quirk in Claude Code's sandbox.

Examples:

- assistant: *builds a test binary*
  assistant: "Let me use the qemu-runner agent to execute the binary and check the output"

- user: "Run this ELF at VLEN=512"
  assistant: "I'll use the qemu-runner agent to run it" (Tools: Bash, Read) (Tools: Bash)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- cc-log: Lightweight system log to record all Claude Code behavior (tool use, subagent creation, compaction, permissions, session lifecycle) for analysis. Use when the user wants to enable/disable behavior logging, analyze Claude Code session logs, list saved logs, or understand Claude Code's tool usage patterns. Trigger on: "cc-log", "behavior log", "system log", "record behavior", "log enable", "log disable", "analyze log".
- iree-optimizer: Agentic per-dispatch tile-size tuner for IREE CPU codegen on RISC-V. Keeps IREE's chosen pipeline (CPUDoubleTilingExpert / CPUConvTileAndDecomposeExpert / CPUBufferOpsTileAndVectorize) and only overrides the root linalg op's lowering_config<tile_sizes = [...]>. Each round reads the best-so-far RISC-V assembly (LMUL, VLmax, register spills) to ground the next tile-size proposal; pre-compile divisibility gate ensures tiles divide their parent extents (no tail loop); a post-compile check of the IR after iree-codegen-generic-vectorization confirms no tail/masked main path. Compiles via iree_tuner.py, benchmarks on FPGA, iterates. Use whenever the user mentions tuning IREE dispatch tile sizes, agentic tile search, or wants to replace GA-based tile-size search with LLM-driven search. Trigger on "iree optimize", "optimize dispatch", "tile tune", or references to dispatch .mlir files for performance tuning.
- libnn-optimizer: Autonomous optimization workflow for libnn RISC-V neural network library functions
in the agentic_libnn_opt project. Use this skill when the user wants to optimize a
libnn function for FPGA performance, run the libnn optimization loop, validate the
optimization config, parse FPGA hardware features, extract shapes from perf test files,
or manage the optimization state machine. Trigger when: user mentions "optimize",
"libnn", "FPGA perf", "optimization loop", "validate config",
"phase gather/baseline/iterate/evaluate", "perf test", or references opt/config.toml,
opt/state.json, or any libnn function optimization task.
- libnn-wiki-writer: Internal style guide for writing docs/wiki/ pages during /libnn-optimizer learn phase. Not a standalone skill -- read by the optimize agent.
- mlir-transform-writer: Write MLIR transform dialect scripts that directly control IR lowering - tiling, fusion, vectorization, bufferization, GPU thread mapping, shared memory promotion, and more. Use this skill whenever someone asks to generate, write, or modify a transform dialect script, transform library, codegen strategy, or tuning spec in MLIR. Also trigger when the request involves composing IR transformations for linalg ops, controlling IREE codegen pipelines via transform dialect, or replacing annotation-only configs with full transform strategies. Covers both upstream MLIR transform ops and IREE-specific extensions.
- skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- spec-human: Create a human-reviewable architecture spec using a 6-section template (Summary, Background, Architecture, Interface, Edge Cases, Alternatives) BEFORE implementing a non-trivial design. Triggered explicitly via /spec-human <topic>, or when the user says "write a human spec", "create a review-ready design doc", "spec this out for review", or "I need a spec for X before we build it". Produces an ASCII markdown document at ./specs/<slug>.md aimed at peer engineers and tech leads who need to validate core architecture and trade-offs in 5 minutes. Do NOT auto-trigger on general design questions or coding tasks - this is a deliberate review gate that only fires on explicit request. input.description: Show files changed in rv32 support commit

content.content:
commit ee3addad647be7aaece95ff065fb18d3cc6ec496
Author: Nick Hung <nick@andestech.com>
Date:   Mon Jun 29 21:34:44 2026 +0800

    feat: rv32 support across run, runtime, and fixtures
    
    andesim now treats rv32 as a first-class peer of rv64, driven by the ELF's
    class byte (e_ident[EI_CLASS]). See docs/rv32_ROADMAP.md.
    
    Run dispatch (driver/):
    - elf_xlen() reads an ELF's width (32/64). fast auto-picks
      qemu-system-riscv32/64 from the ELF (explicit --engine wins + warns on a
      conflict); cycle and hybrid reject an ELF whose class != the engine's xlen
      via one shared elf_engine_arch_error -- a clear up-front message instead of
      the engine's cryptic "not of ELFCLASSxx".
    
    Dual-arch runtime (runtime/, config, scripts):
    - runtime/Makefile parameterized by ARCH: rv64 -> build/runtime,
      rv32 -> build/runtime/rv32 (rv32gc/ilp32d, riscv32-unknown-elf-).
    - Real rv64-isms fixed: vplat_syscalls.c L2-cache flush guarded to rv64
      (#if __riscv_xlen==64); handler.c trap CSRs made XLEN-wide, which also fixes
      latent rv64 mepc/mtval truncation and the interrupt-bit test.
    - HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32 config var (a second, separate toolchain);
      build_runtime.sh builds both arches (and its stale artifact names fixed);
      build_all.sh runtime delegates to it.
    
    rv32 fixtures (tests/fixtures/):
    - make rv32 -> rv32_spin (asm) + rv32_c_hello (C, links the rv32 runtime),
      reusing existing sources.
    
    Docs: USER_GUIDE sec 1.3 (two toolchains) + new sec 5.1 (rv32 link command and
    the arch-match rules).
    
    Tested (TDD, RED first): elf_xlen unit (driver/elf_syms_test.cpp);
    test_andes_sim_arch_match.sh (both arch directions, incl. a real rv32_c_hello
    run on qemu-system-riscv32); test_andes_sim_runtime_dual.sh (both runtime
    classes). rv64 fixtures and the fast/cycle/hybrid suites stay green.
    Behavioral change.
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.8 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

content.content:
### 2.5.1 Running on WSL2 and macOS

The hybrid handoff needs both legs (QEMU and vsim) on **one Linux
kernel**, with the mmap file on a filesystem local to that kernel.
That rule decides what each OS needs:

**Linux** -- native, nothing to do.

**Windows (WSL2)** -- works as Linux; two caveats:

- Keep the repo and the mmap dirs on the ext4 side (`~/...`), never
  under `/mnt/c` (drvfs is slow and `MAP_SHARED` is not coherent there).
- `/dev/shm` is capped by the WSL VM memory. Raise `memory=` in
  `%UserProfile%\.wslconfig` if tier 1 is too small -- or just let the
  tier list fall through to `~/.cache/andesim`.

`./andesim doctor` checks both (see the `mmap tiers:` section and the
WSL warnings at the end of its report).

**macOS** -- run-only. vsim is a Linux binary, so `./andesim` re-execs
the run inside a prebuilt Linux runtime image in the podman machine VM;
the mmap lives inside that VM (the container's `/dev/shm`), never on a
virtiofs mount. One-time setup:

```sh
brew install podman
podman machine init --memory 4096   # the VM hosts /dev/shm (tier 1)
podman machine start
podman pull <runtime image>         # or load a CI-built andesim-runtime:latest
./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --mem-size 256M my.elf
```

Knobs: `ANDESIM_IMAGE` (image name, default `andesim-runtime:latest`),
`ANDESIM_SHM_SIZE` (container `/dev/shm`, default `3g`),
`ANDESIM_CONTAINER_ENGINE` (podman/docker). Your current directory is
bind-mounted at the same path, so relative ELF paths and output files
work; builds (`scripts/build_all.sh`) stay Linux-only. The image is built on
Linux from `Dockerfile.runtime` (it bakes a fully built repo at
`/opt/hybrid_sim`); Apple Silicon runs the x86-64 image under emulation,
so expect slower wall-clock than a Linux host.

### 2.6 Orchestrator plan YAML (used by archive/replay)

For checkpoint workflows you describe a multi-step plan in YAML and
hand it to the orchestrator:

```yaml
session:
  mem_size: 134217728            # 128 MB shared mmap
  mmap_path: null                # null -> mktemp in /dev/shm
  elf: tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf

steps:
  - model: qemu
    trigger: { kind: marker }       # marker trigger; can also be { kind: pc, enter: 0x... }
    on_exit: { archive_as: "snap/0" }
```

Run it:

```sh
python3 -m orchestrator.main run plan.yaml \
  --project-root . --workdir /tmp/run --archive-root /tmp/archives
```

Replay:

```sh
python3 -m orchestrator.main replay-checkpoint /tmp/archives/snap/0 \
  --resume-with vsim --project-root . --workdir /tmp/replay
```

### 2.5.1 Running on WSL2 and macOS

The hybrid handoff needs both legs (QEMU and vsim) on **one Linux
kernel**, with the mmap file on a filesystem local to that kernel.
That rule decides what each OS needs:

**Linux** -- native, nothing to do.

**Windows (WSL2)** -- works as Linux; two caveats:

- Keep the repo and the mmap dirs on the ext4 side (`~/...`), never
  under `/mnt/c` (drvfs is slow and `MAP_SHARED` is not coherent there).
- `/dev/shm` is capped by the WSL VM memory. Raise `memory=` in
  `%UserProfile%\.wslconfig` if tier 1 is too small -- or just let the
  tier list fall through to `~/.cache/andesim`.

`./andesim doctor` checks both (see the `mmap tiers:` section and the
WSL warnings at the end of its report).

**macOS** -- run-only. vsim is a Linux binary, so `./andesim` re-execs
the run inside a prebuilt Linux runtime image in the podman machine VM;
the mmap lives inside that VM (the container's `/dev/shm`), never on a
virtiofs mount. One-time setup:

```sh
brew install podman
podman machine init --memory 4096   # the VM hosts /dev/shm (tier 1)
podman machine start
podman pull <runtime image>         # or load a CI-built andesim-runtime:latest
./andesim run --mode hybrid --trigger marker --mem-size 256M my.elf
```

Knobs: `ANDESIM_IMAGE` (image name, default `andesim-runtime:latest`),
`ANDESIM_SHM_SIZE` (container `/dev/shm`, default `3g`),
`ANDESIM_CONTAINER_ENGINE` (podman/docker). Your current directory is
bind-mounted at the same path, so relative ELF paths and output files
work; builds (`scripts/build_all.sh`) stay Linux-only. The image is built on
Linux from `Dockerfile.runtime` (it bakes a fully built repo at
`/opt/hybrid_sim`); Apple Silicon runs the x86-64 image under emulation,
so expect slower wall-clock than a Linux host.

### 2.6 Orchestrator plan YAML (used by archive/replay)

For checkpoint workflows you describe a multi-step plan in YAML and
hand it to the orchestrator:

```yaml
session:
  mem_size: 134217728            # 128 MB shared mmap
  mmap_path: null                # null -> mktemp in /dev/shm
  elf: tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_matmul.elf

steps:
  - model: qemu
    trigger: { kind: marker }       # marker trigger; can also be { kind: pc, enter: 0x... }
    on_exit: { archive_as: "snap/0" }
```

Run it:

```sh
python3 -m orchestrator.main run plan.yaml \
  --project-root . --workdir /tmp/run --archive-root /tmp/archives
```

Replay:

```sh
python3 -m orchestrator.main replay-checkpoint /tmp/archives/snap/0 \
  --resume-with vsim --project-root . --workdir /tmp/replay
```

content.content:
### 5.1 rv32 and rv64

The runtime builds for **both** widths from two toolchains (`HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN`
= rv64, `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32` = rv32; section 1.3). `scripts/build_all.sh
runtime` builds both when `HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32` is set:

- rv64 -> `build/runtime/` (link `-B build/runtime`, as above).
- rv32 -> `build/runtime/rv32/` (link `-B build/runtime/rv32`).

The rv32 link is the same shape with the rv32 compiler and `-march=rv32gc
-mabi=ilp32d`:

```sh
"$HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN32/bin/riscv32-unknown-elf-gcc" -march=rv32gc -mabi=ilp32d -O1 \
  -B build/runtime/rv32 -specs=andesim.specs your_prog.c -o your_prog.elf
```

**The driver follows the ELF's width.** `run` reads the ELF's class
(rv32/rv64) and:

- **fast** auto-selects `qemu-system-riscv32` or `qemu-system-riscv64` to match
  the ELF -- no flag needed (an explicit `--engine qemu32`/`qemu64` overrides,
  with a warning if it disagrees with the ELF).
- **cycle** / **hybrid** reject an ELF whose width does not match the chosen
  engine, up front, instead of a cryptic failure deep inside the engine:

  ```
  $ ./andesim run --mode cycle --engine vsim:ax45mpv_premium prog_rv32.elf
  andesim run --mode cycle: ELF is rv32 but engine 'vsim:ax45mpv_premium' is rv64
    -- pick a matching engine or an rv64 ELF
  ```

See `docs/andesim_runtime_tutorial.ipynb` for a step-by-step walkthrough
of what the two flags do, what to avoid, and how to add ROI markers and RVV.

Ready-made fixtures: `vplat_hello.elf` (stdio + exit), `vplat_exit41.elf`
(exit-code propagation), `vplat_file.elf` (HTIF file io); they are built
with exactly the two-flag command above. Per-feature smoke tests live in
`tests/vplat/test_vplat_f1..f9.sh`.

Notes:

- **Exit codes** stay below 256; the write to `0xe0080000` terminates the
  simulation and becomes the simulator process exit code on both engines
  (magic commands `0x01234567/68/71` map to 0, `0x01234569/70` to 1).
- **File io** is host-passthrough: paths resolve relative to the engine
  process cwd; the QEMU device mirrors vsim's `sys_call.hpp` table
  byte-for-byte (newlib->Linux `O_*` translation, `st_mode`/`st_size`-only
  stat writeback).
- **ROI markers are safe in vplat binaries.** The markers are RISC-V HINTs
  (`slti x0, x0, 0x5A0/0x5A1` -- rd=x0 discards the result), so they execute
  as NOPs on every engine and on silicon: one marker ELF runs standalone on
  fast/cycle AND drives `--trigger marker` on hybrid. Get them from
  `#include <andesim/ROI.h>` (`andesim_ROI_begin()/end()`; the header
  rides the same `-B build/runtime` flag). For binaries you cannot edit,
  delimit the ROI with PC symbols and `--trigger pc` instead (see
  `tests/fixtures/vplat_hello.c`: `say_hello` / `vplat_roi_end`).
- A `printf` inside the measured window now works (the UART is modeled and
  its MMIO cost is real), but it still adds those UART cycles to the figure -
  keep measured kernels I/O-free when you care about clean numbers.
- `docs/andes_sim_tutorial.ipynb` sections 2, 3 and 4d run the same
  `hello.elf` through all three models.

content.content:
build/runtime/rv32/include/andesim/ROI.h
=== ROI.h ===
/* andesim/ROI.h - ROI markers for cycle measurement.
 *
 * andesim_ROI_begin()/andesim_ROI_end() delimit the region of
 * interest. On `--mode hybrid --trigger marker` the simulator switches
 * QEMU -> vsim at begin and drains at end; the reported window_cycles
 * covers exactly the span between the two markers.
 *
 * The markers are RISC-V HINT instructions (slti x0, x0, 0x5A0/0x5A1).
 * An rd=x0 instruction discards its result, so each marker is an
 * architectural NOP on every conforming core: the SAME binary runs
 * unmodified on --mode fast, --mode cycle, and real silicon.
 *
 * Cycle-attribution contract: the "memory" clobber pins memory accesses
 * across the marker but NOT register-only computation -- the compiler may
 * hoist a register-resident kernel out of the span. To keep a kernel
 * inside the measured window, anchor it through memory (read inputs /
 * write outputs inside the span) or call it as a noinline function
 * between the markers.
 */

#ifndef ANDESIM_ROI_H
#define ANDESIM_ROI_H

static inline void andesim_ROI_begin(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("slti x0, x0, 0x5A0\n" ::: "memory");
}

static inline void andesim_ROI_end(void)
{
  __asm__ __volatile__("slti x0, x0, 0x5A1\n" ::: "memory");
}

#endif /* ANDESIM_ROI_H */
